read: A quieter, data-led Tuesday after Monday's heavy news flow. The two big prints were in genetic medicine. Beam's risto-cel met its pivotal endpoint, setting up the first base-editing BLA by year-end, and PepGen nearly doubled on the cleanest DM1 splicing data yet. Commercial execution is still being punished: Legend fell about 16% even though Carvykti grew 36%, because management said Street numbers for Q4 and 2027 sit at the top of its scenarios. That echoes Ionis's sell-off on Monday. Macro was a mild headwind (S&P 500 -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.7% on a firmer core inflation print), and policy noise is shifting from executive action to congressional oversight: Democrats want the unredacted MFN deals before they take committee gavels in January. Capital and attention remain on de-risked late-stage assets and oligo/editing platforms, while private financing was thin on the day.

items.headline: Beam Therapeutics: risto-cel (BEAM-101) meets its primary endpoint in the pivotal BEACON study in severe sickle cell disease; BLA as early as year-end 2026
items.detail: 49 patients dosed (39 adults, 10 adolescents) at the 20 Oct cutoff, 31 of them evaluable for VF12 (no severe VOCs for 12+ consecutive months). All secondary endpoints and the primary safety endpoints were met at the interim. Beam has not yet disclosed the responder rate or detailed safety, and H.C. Wainwright flags those as the next focus; earlier-cutoff data come as an ASH oral (12-15 Dec). This would be the first BLA for a base editor, and it competes with Vertex/CRISPR's Casgevy on a busulfan-conditioned ex vivo market that has launched slowly. The read-through to Beam's in vivo programmes (BEAM-302, BEAM-304) matters more than SCD economics.

items.headline: PepGen closes up about 93% on Phase 2 FREEDOM2-DM1 data for PGN-EDODM1 in myotonic dystrophy type 1
items.detail: At 10 mg/kg (n=6), mean splicing correction was 46.5% at week 13. Five of six patients exceeded 20% and four exceeded 50%. Video hand-opening time improved 3.9s vs 0.2s on placebo, and grip strength rose about 16%. There were no SAEs or DLTs; transient urine-protein rises after the first dose faded with later doses. The 12.5 mg/kg cohort is fully enrolled, with data in 1H27. This is the strongest splicing number in DM1 so far, and it raises the bar for Dyne's DYNE-101 and the other oligo-conjugate DM1 programmes.

items.headline: Legend Biotech falls about 16.5% intraday despite Carvykti sales of about $710m (+36% y/y) and a second profitable quarter
items.detail: US sales were $472m (+19% y/y, flat q/q), and ex-US grew 86%. Legend's net income was $51.7m, and gross margin was 58%, with Q4 guided to the high 50s. The CFO said Q4 and 2027 consensus sit at the high end of internal scenarios, citing slower ex-US launches and slower US earlier-line share gains; 2L/3L patients reached 50% of US apheresis. Bispecific competition is rising. J&J is the partner.

items.headline: Mirum: brelovitug hits in AZURE-4, its second pivotal HDV trial; FDA submission planned for 2027
items.detail: Topline efficacy figures are not yet public. Hepatitis delta is now a three-way race: Gilead's Hepcludex is on market, Vir's tobevibart/elebsiran hit Phase 3 on Saturday, and Mirum is positioning brelovitug as commercially differentiated.

items.headline: House Democrats request unredacted MFN pricing agreements from every company that signed one
items.detail: Letters went out on Monday, and Endpoints reads them as groundwork for subpoenas once Democrats hold committee gavels in January. Recipients include BMS, Pfizer, Lilly and Novo. Taken with BIO's GLOBE lawsuit, this puts the MFN framework under legal and political scrutiny at once, although BioPharma Dive's analysts see the "blue wave" as net positive for the sector.

items.headline: White House presses ahead with Heidi Overton's nomination as FDA commissioner before the lame-duck window closes
items.detail: Cassidy and Murkowski are the swing votes. A confirmed commissioner would end the post-Makary leadership vacuum, while a stalled nomination would leave the agency rudderless into a Democratic-controlled House.

items.headline: Altimmune: RECLAIM Phase 2 of pemvidutide in alcohol use disorder gets an AASLD late-breaker; end-of-Phase 2 FDA meeting set for December
items.detail: Heavy-drinking days per week fell by 4.2 on pemvidutide vs 2.75 on placebo, and PEth fell 38% vs a 5.9% rise. William Blair expects a capital raise before a pivotal AUD programme.

items.headline: ImmunityBio: Q3 revenue of $48.8m vs about $59.2m consensus, its first miss in six quarters; stock down nearly 19% to nine-month lows
Structure Therapeutics: Phase 3 ACCOMPLISH topline for oral GLP-1 aleniglipron guided to 2H28; about $1.2bn cash funds operations through 2028
items.detail: T2D, body-composition and SWITCH readouts are due in Q4, with posters at ObesityWeek on 15 Nov.

items.headline: Vertex's Crinetics unit is cutting 78 roles (about 13%), mainly corporate functions, two months after the roughly $10bn deal closed
Coherus Oncology cuts about 30% of staff, its second 30% cut in under two years, to focus its combination on esophageal cancer
items.detail: The cut saves about $6m in quarterly core burn.

items.headline: BIO unveils "BioAdvance", a seven-part plan to keep the US ahead of China
items.detail: It proposes a White House Office of Biotechnology, centralised trial approvals and more flexible first-in-human rules. It includes no dollar asks.

items.headline: PsiThera (Roivant spinout) raises $25m for oral I&I small molecules
items.detail: Round and investors were not disclosed; the targets are in the TNF superfamily.

items.headline: Neobe raises about $6.8m seed for engineered bacteria to break down tumour barriers
